Assessment (updated with FSR lens): The statement balances solid labor market momentum and steady real activity against inflation running below the 2 percent objective, consistent with New Keynesian and inflation-forecast-targeting guidance to keep policy accommodative while inflation expectations remain anchored. Hurricanes are treated as temporary supply shocks to be looked through.

Financial Stability Report insights tilt the assessment modestly more hawkish: accommodative financial conditions and elevated asset valuations, alongside pockets of leverage and risk-taking, argue for maintaining credibility and gradually removing accommodation to limit buildup of vulnerabilities. That backdrop validates the Committee’s signaling of “gradual increases” and ongoing balance sheet normalization even with near-term inflation softness.

Net tone: slightly positive/hawkish, nudged a bit more hawkish by financial stability considerations.
